title: Federal central fill pharmacy: definition, authorization, registration and who may fill
subtopic: DEA central fill definition and registration
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1300.01 a central fill pharmacy means a pharmacy which is permitted by the state in which it is located to prepare controlled substances orders for dispensing pursuant to a valid prescription transmitted to it by a registered retail pharmacy and to return the labeled and filled prescriptions to the retail pharmacy for delivery to the ultimate user; it is deemed authorized to fill prescriptions on behalf of a retail pharmacy only if the retail pharmacy and central fill pharmacy have a contractual relationship providing for such activities or share a common owner. The registration table in 21 CFR 1301.13(e)(1) places Central Fill Pharmacy within the dispensing or instructing business activity for Schedules II-V and states that a retail pharmacy may perform central fill pharmacy activities. Under 21 CFR 1306.06 a prescription for a controlled substance may only be filled by a pharmacist acting in the usual course of professional practice and either registered individually or employed in a registered pharmacy, a registered central fill pharmacy, or a registered institutional practitioner, and under 21 CFR 1306.05(f) the corresponding liability for filling a prescription not prepared in the form DEA regulations prescribe rests on the pharmacist, including a pharmacist employed by a central fill pharmacy. Under 21 CFR 1305.03(d) delivery from a central fill pharmacy to a retail pharmacy does not require a DEA Form 222 or electronic order, and under 21 CFR 1306.26(g) central fill pharmacies may not dispense controlled substances to a purchaser at retail under that section.
exam_relevance: Tests the federal frame a Massachusetts pharmacy relies on when a central fill pharmacy prepares its controlled-substance prescriptions: state permission, a contract or common owner, DEA registration, and return of the filled prescription to the retail pharmacy.
